blocks.x: I’ve got it, bad memory for that particular date. It was all bass clarinet. About three or four weeks before the date I went to the music store and got a bass clarinet and mouth piece and started wood shedding, and that was the only recording I made with bass clarinet through the whole thing – and – it’s one of the few five star ratings I got on these…
What do you attribute that to?
It was that different and it was into the modern concept of playing.
Was it difficult to pick it up to make that transition?

Not really, not really. But that was the only time I ever played bass clarinet on a recording and I did play it for a few months after that, but then I realized when I was playing in different clubs that nobody particularly cared if I played it or not. It didn’t, the album didn’t sell. The album later on was released, and I think I mentioned this before, was re-released and it was Art Blakey, Blues Bag - Art Blakey’s album – featuring – Buddy DeFranco on bass clarinet.
That’s the one. [laughter] Sound Engineer: We just need to take a pause here. And, we’re rolling.
